chapters.title: The AI money is leaving
chapters.md:
**Where we are:** This is where the story starts. Money has been draining out of the market for a week: Oct 7 and 8 saw 62% and 58% of dollar volume in falling stocks, a brief bounce on Oct 9, then two more selling days, and the last five official sessions netted about −$229B. Today was the heaviest yet: about 72% of dollars traded in falling stocks (net roughly −$275B), only 9 stocks on the live list rose 4%+ against 241 that fell 4%+, and just 16 of 102 sub-themes finished green. The S&P lost 1.1% and the Nasdaq-100 2.0%, while the equal-weight S&P only fell 0.6%: the damage is concentrated in the big AI names.

**What it means:** This is money leaving, not just rotating. The selling hit AI infrastructure hardest (Neoclouds −11.6%, Custom Silicon −8.1%, AI Servers −7.6%, Optical −7.4%, Memory −4.6%, Hyperscalers −3.5%), while the only real inflows went to defensive corners: Large-cap Pharma +2.2%, Defense Primes +2.2%, Managed Care +1.7%, Integrated Oil +0.8%, Utilities +0.4%. VIX jumped 10.5% and Treasuries rose. Breadth is washed out (T2108 32, 10-day ratio 0.86), so the setup for a breadth thrust is in place, but the regime is still choppy and the playbook still says weak breadth.

**Scenario A — money keeps leaving:** Watch for another day with 60%+ of dollars in falling stocks and new lows outnumbering new highs. Here history has an important twist: heavy-selling days inside a streak have tended to come right before a snapback (SPY median +1.7% over the next 10 sessions, n 18), and the groups sold hardest led it. So don't press shorts into days like today. Keep size small, hold only relative strength with leaders (Managed Care, Integrated Oil, Refiners), and build a snapback list from the 60-day leaders sold hardest this week: Custom Silicon, Semicap Equipment, Memory & Storage, AI Drug Discovery.

**Scenario B — money comes back:** The sign is a day with 40% or less of dollars in falling stocks, more stocks up 4% than down, and the thrust gauge waking up. Where it goes matters. If the sold AI groups bounce hardest, that's the snapback; trade the strongest names that held their trend, and expect it to be quick. If a calm "money is back" day prints, history says that bounce has usually already run (sold groups ≈ flat afterwards, n 9) and the durable leaders are the groups that held up: right now that's oil (Refiners, Shale, Integrated), Managed Care, Tower REITs and insurers. A breadth thrust would flip the playbook to "press".

**Leaderboard:**
- Refiners stay #1 (Strength 99) with MPC, VLO, DINO, CVI and PBF all RS 98; Tankers #3; Shale E&P jumped from #30 to #7 and Integrated Oil from #25 to #10 in five sessions.
- Energy and tankers now hold four of the top ten spots; AI Drug Discovery moved into the top 10 today as Shale slipped to #11.
- Managed Care and Integrated Oil met all four ignition checks on today's prices (Grade B: leaders, but breadth isn't strong).

**Your trades:**
- CDNA (pick #1) closed 4% under its $67.39 trigger: no entry yet. ATRC held up (+0.8%).
- CRWD is about 1% above its ~$249 stop in a group being sold; CLMT (oil) is the best of the open trades.

**Next tell:** Does Large-cap Pharma follow through (it missed a Day 1 only on volume)? Does Managed Care's Oct 9 Day 1 hold? And do the AI groups keep falling on heavy volume, or does tomorrow bring the snapback history points to?

Five sessions have now drained about −$384B. T2108 is down to 28 and the dashboard calls the regime **washed out**. The snapback history points to has not started: Nasdaq-100 futures are −1.2% this morning while Russell 2000 (+0.3%) and Dow (+0.3%) futures are green.

**Why it's moving:**
- **AI infrastructure (Neoclouds, Custom Silicon, Optical, Memory): catalyst, macro + credit.** September CPI came in at 3.7% vs 3.6% expected, reviving Fed-hike bets, and the cost of funding the AI build-out is in question: CoreWeave's credit spread broke 1,000 bp with its 2032 bonds near 16% ([TradingKey](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262218623-us-premarket-tsmc-record-profit-chip-stocks-fall-nvidia-micron-ppi-tradingkey)). TSMC's record quarter didn't stop it; Korea's KOSPI fell almost 8% overnight ([Invezz](https://invezz.com/news/2026/10/15/nasdaq-futures-crash-380-points-5-things-to-know-before-wall-street-opens-on-oct-15/)). Memory gaps −4.9%, Optical −4.3%.
- **Nuclear (SMR) and Quantum: catalyst.** The 10-year yield hit 5.26% after CPI, hitting companies whose profits are years away ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/14/nuscale-power-falls-7-as-10-year-treasury-yield-climbs-to-5-26-energy-fuels-drops-9-oklo-slides-5/)). - **Managed Care: catalyst, confirmed by price.** Humana jumped 16% on better Medicare star ratings ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/09/humana-soars-16-on-improved-medicare-advantage-star-ratings-cvs-slides-3-unitedhealth-holds-steady/)), then UnitedHealth beat and raised ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/13/unitedhealth-rises-4-on-earnings-beat-and-raised-full-year-outlook-humana-advances-2/)). The Oct 9 Day 1 held (+5.0% at day 3) and the group IGNITED yesterday.
- **Integrated Oil: catalyst.** Reported Iranian attacks on ships in Hormuz lifted crude ([Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/14/oil-prices-rise-after-reported-attacks-on-ships-in-strait-of-hormuz)). Also an ignition yesterday.
- **Tower REITs and Social & Ad: catalyst, not shelter.** SpaceX's ~$8B 800 MHz spectrum buy sent towers up 6–13% on Oct 9 ([Wireless Estimator](https://wirelessestimator.com/articles/2026/spacexs-8-billion-800-mhz-buy-sends-crown-castle-american-tower-and-sba-shares-soaring-on-a-tenant-that-hasnt-signed-a-lease/)); Bumble near a $1B take-private ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/10/62310063/bumble-stock-jumps-as-dating-app-nears-1-billion-take-private-deal)). One-offs.
- **Gold (+1.6% futures) is shelter; Fertilizers (−7.5% gap) are unexplained** (no news found).

**What it means:** This is a rates-and-credit repricing of debt-funded AI, not a broad panic; money hides in groups with their own news (insurers, oil) and gold. Breadth is washed out and a thrust setup is live, but the Act gate is off (10-day ratio peak 1.03), so the playbook stays weak breadth: Flags and VCPs only.

**Scenario A — money keeps leaving:** Another 60%+ day keeps A. History says heavy-selling days inside a streak tend to precede a snapback (SPY median +1.7% over 10 sessions, n 18), with the sold-hardest groups leading. Don't press shorts here. Build the snapback list from 60-day leaders sold hardest: Custom Silicon (−17.3% vs SPY), Semicap (−13.7%), Memory (−12.7%), AI Servers (−7.3%).

**Scenario B — money comes back:** Needs a day at 40% or less in falling stocks. If it comes with AI ripping, that's the snapback: quick trades in names that held trend. If it's a calm day, history says follow what held up (+1.7% vs SPY, n 9): Managed Care, Integrated Oil, Shale, Refiners.

**Leaderboard:**
- Refiners #1 (99.3) with MPC, VLO, PSX, DINO; Tankers #2; Integrated Oil jumped #22 → #9 and Shale #16 → #8 in five sessions.
- AI Servers fell to #3 after −9.0% yesterday; MRNA (RS 99) is the strongest non-energy name.

**Your trades:**
- CRWD is sitting on its ~$249 stop in a group being sold; respect it. CDNA (open) is ~2% above its $63.41 stop.
- Picks ABCL ($13.06) and CDNA ($67.73) need a trigger; with NQ −1.2%, no fill is fine.

**Next tell:** 8:30 PPI and retail sales (another hot print feeds the yields story); do Memory and Neoclouds close off their lows; do Managed Care and Integrated Oil hold their ignitions.

**How markets work:** *Long-duration stocks feel rates first.* A stock's value is today's price of profits expected in the future; when the 10-year yield rises, profits far away are discounted harder. So pre-profit stories (SMR, quantum, neoclouds) fall most on a hot inflation print, while insurers and oil producers earning cash now barely notice. It breaks when growth news overwhelms rates. Trade it: on hot-CPI days, stop buying dips in "future" groups and look at cash-now leaders.

chapters.title: Selling pauses; a broad bounce leaves chips behind
chapters.md:
**Where we are:** This morning's chapter had Scenario A in charge, with Nasdaq futures −1.2% after hot CPI. The day flipped. A second hot print (PPI +6.3% a year) hit early, then the 10-year yield fell ~9 bp to 5.10% and buyers stepped in everywhere except chips ([ts2](https://ts2.tech/en/dow-jumps-1-1-russell-2000-rises-1-4-as-broad-rotation-beats-tech/)). On Google closing prices only about 45% of dollar volume sat in falling stocks (net about +$72B), 183 stocks rose 4%+ against 35 that fell, and 107 of 131 sub-themes closed green. SPY +0.3% and QQQ −0.1%, but equal-weight RSP and IWM both +1.4%. The selling paused. It didn't reverse: the engine moves to **W**.

**Why it's moving:**
- **Semis, Custom Silicon, AI hardware (biggest outflows): catalyst, rates.** The hot PPI revived fears that borrowing costs will slow AI data-center spending. FormFactor −7.9%, Teradyne −5.1% ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/formfactor-teradyne-applied-materials-amd-173627052.html)), and SMH fell for an eighth straight session ([Invezz](https://invezz.com/news/2026/10/15/servicenow-stock-rises-6-as-investors-rotate-to-enterprise-software-stocks/)). Semicap −3.2%, Custom Silicon −2.5%.
- **Enterprise SaaS (+6.0%): rotation inside tech, plus a catalyst.** Money left indebted AI names for established software. TD Cowen lifted ServiceNow's target to $165, and IGV rose about 1% ([Invezz](https://invezz.com/news/2026/10/15/servicenow-stock-rises-6-as-investors-rotate-to-enterprise-software-stocks/)).
- **Neoclouds (+3.3%): oversold bounce, not news.** CoreWeave fell as much as 10% early on credit worries, then closed +5.9% ([ts2](https://ts2.tech/en/dow-jumps-1-1-russell-2000-rises-1-4-as-broad-rotation-beats-tech/)).
- **IT Services (ignition): catalyst follow-through.** The group has been rerating since Accenture's beat on Oct 1 ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/cognizant-shares-rise-7-2-123306736.html)).
- **Integrated Oil (ignition at the last close): mixed.** WTI rose about 3% on an 8.6M-barrel inventory draw, but energy stocks still fell 1.6% ([ts2](https://ts2.tech/en/dow-jumps-1-1-russell-2000-rises-1-4-as-broad-rotation-beats-tech/)).
- **Launch & Space (net outflow despite +2.5%): catalyst.** Rocket Lab fell about 10% premarket after delaying a rocket debut ([TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-oct-15-2026)).
- **Managed Care (fresh Day 1): rotation/shelter.** No fresh news found; background is Humana's Oct 9 star-ratings jump ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/humana-stock-jumps-raised-medicare-134433952.html)).

**What it means:** A broad, equal-weight bounce from a washout, not money returning to AI. Chips are still for sale. The thrust gauge read 3.4× its 40-day average, above the 2.5× "thrust pace," so a breadth thrust may print in the official data overnight. The sold-hardest basket (+1.3%) lagged the held-up basket (+2.2%), so there's no clean winner yet.

**Scenario A — money keeps leaving:** another day at 60%+ falling would put it back on. Stay out of semis until SMH snaps its losing streak.

**Scenario B — money comes back:** needs a close at 40% or less falling. If that comes after today's heavy-selling setup, history says the snapback has usually already run (SPY median −1.2% over 10 sessions, n 9). Follow what held up (IT Services, Consumer Brands, Business Services, Drug Distributors) more than the bounce in Quantum or SMR.

**Leaderboard:**
- Refiners stay #1 (Strength 99.4), but Refiners −2.2% and Integrated Oil −1.1% fell today as money moved to beaten-down groups.
- Enterprise AI Infrastructure (#3) fell another −5.2%; Cybersecurity slid #4 → #10.
- Best stocks: MPC, VLO and PSX in Refiners. MRNA (RS 99) is the lone runner outside oil.

**Your trades:**
- CRWD is about −4.4%, sitting right on its ~249 stop. Respect it.
- CDNA (−4.1%, stop ~63.41) and RNG (−2.2%, stop ~73.58) still hold their stops. ATRC is +2.1%.
- Picks ABCL (trigger 13.06, close 12.37) and CDNA (trigger 67.73) haven't triggered. Only take them if they clear the trigger.

**Next tell:** First, whether tonight's official numbers confirm a breadth thrust. Second, whether tomorrow holds at 40% falling or less (B) or snaps back above 60% (A).

**How markets work:** *A thrust out of a washout is the sellers running out.* When breadth is crushed (T2108 28), most willing sellers have sold. A small piece of good news, like falling yields today, then sends hundreds of stocks up 4%+ at once: shorts cover, and funds sitting in cash buy back in. One such day is a hint, not a signal. On this dashboard, 2.5× pace caught 10 of 13 thrust days but also fired 10 false alarms. Wait for the official print and a follow-through before pressing.

That came one day after the heaviest washout of the week (71.8% falling, 516 down 4%+). Futures are quiet: S&P +0.1%, Nasdaq-100 −0.2%, Russell 2000 +0.2%, the dollar −0.4%.

Reuters also reports investors pushing back on Anthropic's ~$2T IPO valuation ([Investrade](https://investrade.com/morning-preview-october-16-2026/)).
- **Tower REITs (held up, +11.3% vs SPY): catalyst.** SpaceX's ~$8B purchase of 800 MHz spectrum (Oct 9) raised hopes it becomes a new tower tenant. CCI jumped ~13%, AMT ~7% ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/crown-castle-soars-13-spacex-153427812.html)). One-off news, not a trend driver.
- **P&C Insurers (gapping −1.4%): catalyst.** Travelers beat ($9.18 vs $7.36 EPS) but auto policies in force fell 9.2%, and the stock slipped ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/cards/travelers-q3-2026-earnings-trv-01m5268fc8w3z7jbjc3v1jg5gc)).
- **Tankers (+2.2%): catalyst.** International Seaways agreed to buy Bruton, adding four VLCCs ([Investrade](https://investrade.com/morning-preview-october-16-2026/)). **Robotaxi (+3.0%)**: Tesla's new Roadster reveal helps the group (same source); MBLY's +5% gap is **unexplained**.
- **Social & Ad, IT Services, Cannabis: unexplained today.** No fresh news found. IT Services is still riding Accenture's Oct 1 beat; Social & Ad looks like rotation into software-style names away from chips.

**What it means:** A thrust out of a washout is the sellers running out, and now it's official. The playbook flips to **post-thrust**: Focus is Rotation Rookie, Leader Pullback, VCP, Round Number and ATH Magnet; avoid EPs. But the money is not going back to AI. Chips are still falling on rates news and futures still lean against them. The new leadership is software, health care and consumer: four fresh ignitions (Consumer Brands, Drug Distributors, E-Commerce, Managed Care) and five Day 1s (E-Commerce, Waste, Payments, Restaurants, Insurance Brokers).

**Scenario A — money keeps leaving:** another close at 60%+ falling would undo the thrust. Heavy-selling days in a streak have tended to come before a snapback (n 18), so don't short into it. Avoid Neoclouds and Memory while they gap down.

**Scenario B — money comes back:** a close at 40% or less. If it comes now, history says follow what held up (+1.7% vs SPY over 10 sessions, n 9), not the bounce: Enterprise SaaS, IT Services, Managed Care, Consumer Brands. A real chip snapback needs SOXX to break its losing streak first.

**Leaderboard:**
- Refiners stay #1 (97.4) but fell −2.3%. Enterprise SaaS jumped #15 → #2 (+5.7%); Managed Care #42 → #8.
- Best stocks: TEAM and PAYC (SaaS), MPC, CVI, DINO (Refiners), CON (Providers). FIGS (RS 97) leads Consumer Brands.

**Your trades:**
- New picks fit the story: **OSCR** (Rotation Rookie, Managed Care ignition) and **SN** (Round Number, Consumer Brands ignition), both buy at the open.
- CRWD is −6.2%, below its ~$249 stop: it's done. ATRC +2.9%; CDNA (−1.2% / −1.7%) holds above ~$63.4.

**Next tell:** Does today follow through on the thrust (more 4% up than down, under 50% falling)? Do the Day 1s (E-Commerce, Restaurants, Payments) stay above their Oct 15 close for three sessions? And does SOXX snap its streak?

**How markets work:** *After a thrust, leadership usually changes.* When breadth thrusts out of a washout, the new leaders are often not the old ones. Funds that sold the crowded trade (here AI hardware) put cash back into groups that held up and have their own news. That's why a thrust day can lift 376 stocks while chips keep falling. It breaks when the old leaders' fundamentals turn first. Use it by buying setups in the newly igniting groups. On this dashboard, Day 1s that hold three sessions later have returned +3.4% over 20 sessions vs −0.7% for those that fade.

Today SPY fell 1.1%, QQQ 2.5%, but RSP only 0.4%: big funds were cutting their largest AI holdings, not dumping everything. This is general market knowledge, not a dashboard study. It usually means the average stock is fine, but it breaks when the big names drag funds into wider selling (like today's 204 stocks down 4%+). For swing trades, track breadth and RSP, not just the index.

chapters.title: Money comes back to AI hardware on SMCI, SpaceX
chapters.md:

- **What's happening:** For about three weeks money has been moving out of AI hardware (chips, chip equipment, optical, memory, data-center power, neoclouds) and into businesses whose profits don't depend on AI spending: IT services, enterprise software, CROs, consumer brands, staples and rate-sensitive groups. - **Why:** Two worries feed each other. - **How it works:** Funds were crowded in AI hardware after a huge run. When the spending story wobbles they trim those winners and park the money in steady earners that don't need AI capex to grow. Falling yields today (10-year ~4.95%) helped the rate-sensitive side too.
- **Real or seesaw:** A seesaw since Oct 16. The two sides move opposite each other, and the winners give back on the days AI bounces (as on Oct 21 after Super Micro's raise). - **What confirms it / what breaks it:** The real test is next week: the Fed decision and Microsoft + Alphabet earnings on Oct 28, PCE and Amazon on Oct 29. If they confirm capex is still growing and is getting paid back, the AI side snaps back and this trade fades. If they cut capex or the market punishes the spending, the rotation keeps going. Code checks: 3 closes of the ratio under its 20-day average = over; a day with ≤ 40% of dollars in falling stocks = comeback trigger.

**Scenario A — money keeps leaving:** Another 60%+ day, or QQQ breaking lower while IWM and RSP hold, says the chip leaders are not done. **Scenario B — money comes back:** Needs a share at or under 40% again. History: after heavy-selling days in an outflow streak (n 18), sold-hardest groups beat SPY by +4.3% over 10 sessions. That favors the 60-day leaders hit today (Semicap, Optical, AI Servers). But today fell after a calm day, so wait for the snapback to start, not the first dip.

**How markets work:** Gold fell 2.6% on a day the market sold off and bonds rallied. That is not a contradiction. In a sharp selloff, funds that need cash sell what has gone up, and gold is easy to sell. The dollar barely moved, so this was not a fear trade. Falling yields helped rate-sensitive groups. It tends to hold when selling is concentrated in one crowded theme (here AI hardware), and breaks when inflation fear pushes stocks and bonds down together, as on Oct 14–15. **What it means:** The market is no longer rotating cleanly between software and chips. It is repricing anyone whose guidance or cash flow does not match the AI spending story, and paying for plain earnings (food, big pharma, defense). That fits W, not A: breadth under the surface was fine yesterday, but a −2.7% Nasdaq open can flip the share in falling stocks above 60% fast.

**The trade, explained:**
- **What's happening:** money has moved from AI Infrastructure (Bitcoin Miners −32%, Quantum −27%, Neoclouds −26% over 20 sessions) into Identity & Security, CROs, Natural Gas and Defense IT (+16% to +19%), 17 sessions now.

Sold-hardest 60-day leaders to watch: Enterprise SaaS, Social & Ad Platforms, Refiners, IT Services.

**Your trades:**

- Open: SLDE −3.2% (stop ~27.53, closest), CDNA +2.3%, BRZE +0.1%, KNSA +2.7%. RBLX, HPQ, DXC, NTAP are gapping 10%+ lower on your lists.

**How markets work:** Stocks trade on the next quarter, not the last one. Reddit, Twilio and Roblox all beat or met the quarter just reported and still fell 17–23% because their guidance came in under what was already priced in. When a stock has run hard, the market is not asking "was it good?" but "was it better than whispered?" Mondelez and Regeneron show the opposite: a beat plus a steady or raised outlook can still gap up. A swing trader uses it by treating the guide as the signal: a beat with a weak guide in a leader is usually a sell-the-rip or avoid, and a beat with a raise inside a strong group is the one worth the opening-range entry. This is general market knowledge; the dashboard's own evidence is that gap-downs in a group did not keep spreading after earnings clusters (n 200).

**Why it's moving:**
- **Whole market: catalyst plus profit-taking.** The Dow fell about 1,833 points and the Nasdaq closed in correction, under its 200-day average. The chip index (SOX) lost 12.25% and the VIX jumped about 70% to 28 ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-thursday-november-5-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-plunge-chip-stocks-melt-down-193726491.html)). Two drivers: worry that a Democratic Congress slows AI data-center building (UBS put about 30% of expected 2028 additions at risk), and funds selling 2026's biggest winners to lock in gains before year-end ([StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/stock-market-today-live-november-5-2026)). Retail was a net seller too, with no dip-buying.
- **Chips, memory, custom silicon (Memory −18.3%, Custom Silicon −16.5%, Optical −16.1%): sympathy with a group-wide unwind.** Micron −17.5%, AMD −17.3%, Marvell −16.4%, Nvidia −9.3% (StockTitan, same page). Korea's Kospi fell 5.3%, so it was global. No single company report explains it.
- **Semicap (AMAT −13.6%, LRCX −16.4%, KLAC −13.3%, ASML −9.3%) and Foundry (TSM −10.8%): sympathy.** I found no equipment-specific news today; these names were already down 30%+ in a month, so they sold with the chip group.
- **Hyperscalers and software (Hyperscalers −3.8%, Developer & DevOps −15.6%): rotation out of AI.** Palantir fell 10%+ at its lows and Salesforce and Adobe barely moved (Yahoo, same page); Amazon closed −2.2% after trading up pre-market (StockTitan).
- **Gaming (+5.7%): catalyst.** Unity's beat-and-raise lifted its group ([StockStory](https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/u/news/earnings/unity-nyseu-reports-upbeat-q3-2026-stock-jumps-228percent)). **Gold miners (+2.1%): shelter.** Gold rose 0.7% (Yahoo); I found no miner-specific news.
**AI monetizers:** AMZN (added Nov 4, AWS AI run rate over $15B) closed −2.2% against QQQ −6.5%: AI revenue is still being paid for.

**What it means:** This is forced, indiscriminate selling: leaders and laggards fell together and only a few havens held. The dashboard's comeback trigger flipped from met to broken in one session. Rotation is not the story today; the exit door is.

**The trade, explained:**
- **What's happening:** Money has moved from AI Infrastructure (Custom Silicon −37.8%, Neoclouds −36.7% over 20 sessions) into Building Products, IT Services and Insurance Brokers for 20 sessions, a 20-day spread of about 43 points.

Rates near 4.84% on the 10-year still weigh.
- **How it works:** Funds that own the year's winners sell them first when they need cash or want to protect gains, and that sets off group-wide selling. Money lands in earnings that do not depend on AI spending.
- **Real or seesaw:** Seesaw (correlation −0.45; winners gave back on the losers' best days). Past gives-back stretches ended with the losers winning the next 10 sessions in 5 of 6 episodes.
- **What confirms it / breaks it:** Friday's 8:30 AM jobs report (December hike odds were 70.1% per StockTitan). The kill switch is 3 closes under the 20-day average; a return to 40% or less of dollar volume in falling stocks would be the comeback trigger.

**Scenario A — money keeps leaving:** A second heavy day (60%+ in falling stocks) or lows beating highs again. History is context: after heavy days inside an outflow streak (n 18), SPY has tended to rise a median 1.7% over 10 sessions and the sold-hardest groups beat SPY by 4.3% vs 0.5% for the held-up ones. Trade small, no chasing, no new shorts into a VIX of 28.

**Scenario B — money comes back:** Needs 40% or less in falling stocks. The snapback has tended to start in what was sold: Enterprise AI Infrastructure, Cybersecurity Platforms, Data & Observability, Shale E&P. After a calm comeback day, follow what held up.

**Leaderboard:** Official Strength (Nov 4) leaders: Exchanges & Financial Data, Healthcare Providers, IT Services. The four fresh ignitions (Building Products, Packaging, Casinos, Airlines) fell 1–4%, less than the market. 12 of 131 sub-themes rose.

**Next tell:** Friday's jobs report and whether Nasdaq reclaims its 200-day average. Watch the share of dollar volume in falling stocks: under 60% on the next session is a pause. Watch whether KNSA and ANF hold their stops.

**How markets work:** When a crowded winner trade unwinds, correlations jump toward one. Funds sell what they can sell, and that means their best-performing, most liquid names first, not the weakest. That is why leaders fell as hard as laggards today. It usually holds when the trigger is positioning (year-end profit-taking) and breaks when real news changes earnings. The dashboard's evidence says snapbacks have tended to start in what was sold hardest, but the first bounce often retests the low. Swing traders use it by waiting for the share of dollar volume in falling stocks to drop, then buying leaders on their first pullback to the 9/21 EMAs.

**How markets work:** When the VIX falls 22% in a day, that is partly a mechanical unwind (general market knowledge). Funds and dealers hold put options as insurance; as fear fades those hedges shrink, and the stock or futures positions behind them get bought back. That buying lifts everything at once, which is why 119 of 131 sub-themes rose. It usually holds when fear peaked the week before (it did, at VIX 28 Thursday). **How markets work:** Markets often pause before a big data print: traders do not want to hold a big position through a number that can swing rate expectations. The result is thin, flat pre-market trading, and then a sharp move on the release. When yields rise on a hot print, long-duration growth stocks and small caps usually suffer most because their future earnings are discounted harder (general market knowledge). A swing trader uses it by not chasing gaps before 8:30 and waiting for the opening range after the print to show who is really buying.

chapters.md:
**The numbers:** October CPI came in hot. Headline rose 0.4% on the month vs 0.3% expected and 0.6% in September; core rose 0.3% vs 0.2% expected and 0.3% prior ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/10/inflation-just-came-in-hotter-than-expected-that-is-a-warning-to-retirees-that-kevin-warshs-fed-is-not-done-raising-rates/), [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/10/u-s-cpi-rose-stronger-than-expected-0-4-in-october-core-rate-rose-0-3)). No official 12-month rate was published because October 2025 prices were not collected during the shutdown.

**How the market took it:** Small. Since before 8:30, S&P futures are +0.04%, Nasdaq-100 futures +0.10%, Russell 2000 futures +0.01%, the dollar index +0.01%, and 10-year note futures -0.06% (yields up a touch). In the ETFs since 8:24, QQQ is -0.75%, SMH -1.35%, IWM -0.89%, KRE -0.75%, TLT -0.18%, and RSP -0.07%. Futures shrugged; the pre-market ETFs lean lower in growth, chips and small caps.

**What it means today:** A hot print keeps the Fed's December 9 hike on the table; CME FedWatch had about 84% priced before the report (24/7 Wall St.), so this confirms rather than shocks. Higher-for-longer rates hurt long-duration growth, chips, small caps and regional banks most, and favor equal-weight and defensives. It sits awkwardly with branch B, money coming back: the bounce in chips and small caps now has to hold against a rates headwind. Oil is down about 2.4% on the day, which helps the inflation outlook.

**Watch at the open:**
- Do QQQ and SMH hold their pre-market weakness, or does the chips bounce get bought again?
- Do IWM and KRE stay lower than SPY? A small-cap lag confirms the rate worry.

chapters.md:
**Where we are:** Yesterday's loud "money is back" day (19.7% of dollar volume in falling stocks officially) gave way to a giveback. On Google closing prices (estimates; official numbers land overnight) 62% of dollar volume sat in falling stocks, net about -$133B. Stocks up 4%+ numbered 27 against 117 down, only 0.3x the 40-day average. SPY -0.37%, QQQ -0.68%, IWM -0.68%, equal-weight RSP -0.03%, VIX -1.9%. The trade: Consumer over AI Infrastructure, day 23, cooling, still a seesaw. Regime is still Breadth thrust on official numbers.

**Why it's moving:**
- **Whole market (rates): catalyst.** October CPI ran hot (+0.4% vs +0.3% expected; core +0.3% vs +0.2%). The 10-year yield rose 7 bp to 4.93%, traders put about 84% odds on a December hike, and the S&P closed at 7,520.93 ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-november-10-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-inflation-data-cpi-090627830.html)). TLT -1.3% and the dollar (UUP) +0.6% fit. The market had priced much of it, so the damage was mild.
- **Gold and gold miners (Gold Mid-tiers -5.5%, Silver Miners -5.8%): catalyst/sympathy.** Gold slid about 2.1% to roughly $4,053 and silver about 2.8% as the hot CPI pulled a December hike into focus ([USAGold](https://www.usagold.com/daily-precious-metals-market-report-november-10-2026/)). Miners fall harder than the metal. These were last week's best-held groups, so they gave back the most.
- **Chips and AI infrastructure (Optical -4.1%, AI Applications -2.7%): rotation plus company news.** Nvidia fell 5.5% to $168.89 on a second day of fallout from the board's investigation into its CEO ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-november-10-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-inflation-data-cpi-090627830.html)). I could not find a driver specific to optical names; call that unexplained beyond sympathy with Nvidia.
- **Take-Two (Gaming +2.7%): catalyst.** TTWO closed +8.1% to $224.19 ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/cards/tech-took-the-brunt-of-it-again-the-nasdaq-s-0-58-slide-wa-gspc-market-bell-01m73mcg7c8097899kgygay6e7)); a Seeking Alpha headline ties an 8% climb to a GTA VI preorder update ([Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4670143-take-two-interactive-software-climbs-8-percent-on-gta-vi-preorder-update)). I could not open the details to confirm the date, so treat the reason as likely, not certain.

Defensive money may be sheltering here.
- **Natural Gas (+3.6%), Airlines, Solar, Space:** no news I could confirm. Oil (USO) -0.85% helps airlines, but I found nothing dated today. Unexplained.

**What it means:** Rates, not fear, drove the day: yields up, dollar up, gold down, growth lagging. The sold-hardest basket held flat (+0.1%) while last week's winners fell 2.2%. That is the snapback idea still alive inside a down tape.

**The trade, explained:**
- **What's happening:** Money has moved from AI infrastructure (Enterprise AI Infrastructure -32%, Memory -31%, Neoclouds -31% over 20 sessions) to consumer groups (Building Products +25%, Home Improvement +23%), 23 sessions running, cooling.
- **Why:** Funds cut crowded AI-capex winners after the Nov 5 washout, and the market is now arguing over a December Fed hike after hot jobs and CPI. I found no single new driver today beyond the hot CPI ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-november-10-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-inflation-data-cpi-090627830.html)).
- **How it works:** Higher yields cut the value of far-off profits, so growth and chips suffer first, while consumer and health groups with nearer earnings hold up better.
- **Real or seesaw:** A seesaw: on the losers' best days the winners gave back (+0.4% vs SPY -0.5%). In past "gives back" stretches the losers won the next 10 sessions in 5 of 6 episodes.
- **What confirms it / breaks it:** The Fed's December 9 decision. The kill switch is 3 closes under the winners' 20-day average; the comeback trigger is met.

**Scenario A — money keeps leaving:** Another day above 60% falling, or net outflow past about -$200B. Trade small, favor what held up, leave extended names alone (KNSA, KYMR, SN).

**Scenario B — money comes back:** A day at 40% or below. After calm "money is back" days SPY has tended to be lower 10 sessions later (n 9), and what held up did better. Follow strong groups, not the bounce.

**Leaderboard:** CROs lead (Strength 96.9), then AI Drug Discovery (93.3), Life Science Tools (92.6) and Home Improvement (92.4). Health care groups rank four of the top ten. Fresh ignitions: Apparel & Footwear, Airlines; Day 1s: Immunology & Inflammation, Engineering & Construction.

**Your trades:** KNSA pick -3.8% and MRNA -6.8% today; both are tests of the plan, not stops. Open trades KOD +15.4%, SYRE +10.8%, KNSA +3.7%, NIQ +3.5%, all above stops.

**Next tell:** Does breadth stay under 60% falling tomorrow. Do ignitions in Airlines and Apparel get a second green day. Do rate-sensitive groups hold with the 10-year near 5%.

**How markets work:** After a very heavy buying day, a giveback is normal. A thrust day (like Nov 9) pulls in short covering and buyers who were out of the market; the next day often brings profit-taking, and a mild pullback that holds above the thrust day's low usually keeps the move intact. Today's drop was about -0.4%, well short of a break. This is general market knowledge, not a dashboard rule. Swing traders watch whether leaders keep their gains on the quiet day; groups that fall with the tape are weak, groups that hold are where the next leg tends to start.

**What it means:** Today's gap is the seesaw, not a new trend. Yesterday's heavy selling and this gap-up both point to a market that keeps flipping, with no washout in the last 10 sessions and no thrust. The Act gate is on, but the breadth thrust has not come.

**The trade, explained:**
- **What's happening:** Money moved from AI Infrastructure (-32.5% over 20 sessions) to IT Services, Immunology, Home Improvement and Building Products (+19% to +21%) for 24 sessions; the spread is +37.0%.
- **Why:** Capex and spy-probe fears hit AI names, and the CoreWeave beat is the first strong demand data point in a while. No single driver found for the full 24-session rotation beyond what is cited here.

- **Real or seesaw:** Seesaw. On the losers' best days the winners gave back (+0.4%, -0.5% vs SPY). In past "gives back" stretches the losing side won the next 10 sessions in 5 of 6 episodes.

**Scenario A — money keeps leaving:** another day at 60%+ falling after a gap-up would make two heavy days in three. Avoid chasing AI gaps; the bounce would fade like Monday's. Stay with Immunology, IT Services, CROs.

**Scenario B — money comes back:** 40% or less falling with up 4%+ well over down. Snapback goes first to what was sold (Refiners, Enterprise AI Infrastructure, Oil, Cybersecurity), then to what held up, which the evidence says tends to win after the bounce ends.

**Leaderboard:** Top 5: Home Improvement (93.9), Exchanges (93.6), CROs (92.3), IT Services (92.0, up from #12), Hotels & Cruise (91.2). Healthcare Providers jumped #32 to #7. Strongest names: REPL, KOD, ETON (RS 99).

**How markets work:** A supplier's customer reports can move a whole chain. CoreWeave buys chips, memory, servers and power gear, so its spending outlook is revenue for those groups; that's why optical, memory and servers all gap together. It holds when the customer raises guidance with real backlog. It breaks if the customer is funding growth with debt that investors stop financing. For a swing trader: watch the customer's report, then trade the strongest supplier after its first pullback.
